data.gender_notes: Danvika is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Name Danvika is derived from the Sanskrit term ‘Danu’ which refers to the Goddess Danu. The name signifies the victory of the Goddess Danu. This name is often used in Hindu mythology and is considered auspicious. The name Danvika carries the meaning “Goddess Danu's victory” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Danvika usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess danu's victory and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the victory of divine over the material

historical_references.reference: Danvika is mentioned in the epic Mahabharata as the name of a Yadav prince, the son of King Prasenajit of Hastinapura. He participated in the Kurukshetra War but died during the battle.
historical_references.context: Ancient India, Hindu mythology, Mahabharata epic

historical_references.reference: Danvika is also mentioned in Jain texts as a Jain Tirthankara, or religious leader, who lived in the 12th Arhat-cycle (avasarani) of the Jain cosmology. He is considered to be the 24th Tirthankara in the current Jain tradition.
